faq.question: What is the difference between a curtain wall and other facade systems?
faq.answer: A curtain wall is a non-structural external facade system fixed to the building's main structure. It carries wind loads and its own weight only. It offers design flexibility, faster installation, and superior thermal performance compared to traditional wall systems.

faq.question: How long does it take to install a curtain wall system?
faq.answer: Execution typically ranges from 8 to 20 weeks depending on area and design complexity. Manufacturing takes 4–8 weeks and site installation varies with building height and access conditions.

faq.question: What is the difference between standard and thermally broken aluminium windows?
faq.answer: Thermally broken aluminium windows contain a non-conductive plastic barrier separating the inner and outer profiles, preventing heat transfer and reducing internal condensation in hot and cold climates alike.

faq.question: Is structural glazing safe in high-wind conditions?
faq.answer: Yes, when properly designed. Certified structural silicone can withstand tensile and shear stresses from wind pressure per ASCE 7 or BS 6262. We provide bonded length and thickness calculations for each project based on location and height.

faq.question: How long does it take to fabricate and erect a medium-sized steel warehouse?
faq.answer: A warehouse of 1,000–2,000 m² typically takes 6–10 weeks: 2 weeks for design and approval, 3–4 weeks for fabrication, and 2 weeks for site erection. We provide a detailed Gantt Chart schedule at project inception.
